A-DISPATCH: a SMSP's scheduler issues at most 1 warp instruction a SMSP-cycle, of any kind, uniform included (the SM's 4 partitions each with one warp scheduler and one dispatch unit: Volta-onward architecture whitepapers)

A-TENSOR: the tensor cores do at most the data sheet's dense peak a SM-clock for the form's type, a 2:4 sparse form twice that on its logical k; a form's SMSP-cycles are its MACs over a quarter of it. H100/H200 (whitepaper: twice A100's MMA rate a SM-clock on each type; data sheet 1979 TOPS s8 dense at 1830 MHz, 132 SMs): dense MACs a SM-clock s8 and e4m3 4096, f16/bf16 2048, tf32 1024, the same for wgmma and mma.sync; f64 128 (DMMA, mma.sync .f64: data sheet 67 TFLOPS at the whitepaper's FP64 Tensor Core clock, 1980 MHz; measured at DMMA.16x8x16, RT-ISA-1); no b1 figure (BGMMA, BMMA on DS_issue alone)

A-PIPE: the alu pipe (Nsight Compute: logic, bit manipulation, integer except IMAD/IMUL) at 64 results a SM-clock (CUDA C++ Programming Guide 12.9 'Arithmetic Instructions' throughput table, CC 9.0: 32-bit add, compare/min/max, bitwise, shift), 2 SMSP-cycles a warp instruction

A-PIPE: IMAD at 64 results a SM-clock (CUDA C++ Programming Guide 12.9 'Arithmetic Instructions' throughput table, CC 9.0: 32-bit integer multiply, multiply-add), 2 SMSP-cycles a warp instruction; FFMA at 128 is held by DS_issue
A-PIPE: SHFL at 32 results a SM-clock (CUDA C++ Programming Guide 12.9 'Arithmetic Instructions' throughput table, CC 9.0: warp shuffle), 4 SMSP-cycles a warp instruction

A-UNIFORM, DS-90's one measured row (RT-MACHINE-4): no document states the uniform datapath's rate (Nsight Compute defines the uniform pipe with none), so it is UP's line, 1.96110716 SMSP-cycles a uniform instruction (the fastest form alone at 0.4999 a SMSP-cycle, 2% margin)

TMA bulk-async facet (cp.async.bulk a copy on SASS UBLKCP, cp.reduce.async.bulk.add.u32 a combine on UBLKRED): a data-movement facet bounded by the HBM write path, not the SMSP issue. Saturated alone: 5.016 words a SM-clock a copy (bulkcp), 3.908 a reduce (bulkred); beside the saturated wgmma 3.004 a copy (wgbulk_cp) and 3.002 a reduce (wgbulk_red), each leaving the wgmma at 0.999 of its alone IGMMA rate (0.9993, 0.9996), so a 4 KB bulk op takes no tensor-pipe issue slot. It folds no word (an integer add, not LI's injective absorb), so it opens no cheaper fold route on this device; it prices the receipt bandwidth the LI-CP-W checkpoint minimises (one 4-byte word a warp a segment)

L2 atomic facet: red.global.xor.b32 with a warp's 32 lanes into one word (REDG.E.XOR.STRONG.GPU), the LI-CP-W checkpoint's lane XOR in memory (RT2-HOPPER-1). lirate on all 132 SMs at 2 and 4 warps a SMSP (ck_red, ck_red2 and ck_red8: 1, 2 and 8 REDG a 4096-word unit): the fastest block of any of them takes 295.97 SMSP-cycles a REDG (ck_red8 at 4 warps a SMSP; ck_red 298.5, ck_red2 299.2), 0.43 lane-ops a SM-cycle (the medians 0.30-0.32), less 2%. The unit's lane work hides under it (every fastest block at 296-317 a REDG whatever its LOP3 and IMAD), so it is a facet of its own; REDG's issue slot is left out, which only cheapens it. Shared-memory atomics (red.shared) are not timed and are not on it
